games.title: Life Cycle Sorter
games.skillName: Comparing life cycles of different animal groups
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the differences in the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird
games.instruction: Tap the animal group each life cycle stage belongs to.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how the young are born and how they change as they grow, then try again.

questions.ask: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly
A tadpole growing back legs
A chick hatching from a hard-shelled egg in a nest
A calf drinking its mother's milk
A larva becoming a pupa, then an adult beetle
Frogspawn laid in a pond in spring
Parents feeding nestlings until they can fly
A furry baby fed on milk by its mother

games.title: Material Misfit
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare and group together everyday materials on the basis of their properties, including their hardness, solubility, transparency, conductivity (electrical and thermal), and response to magnets
games.instruction: Tap the material that does not belong with the others.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the property in the question and test each material in your head, then try again.

questions.ask: Which one is NOT attracted to a magnet?
Which one does NOT conduct electricity?
Which one does NOT dissolve in water?
Which one is NOT transparent?
Which one is NOT a good thermal insulator?
Which one is NOT a hard material?
Which one is NOT a reversible change?
Which one is NOT a way to separate a mixture?

games.title: Orbit Truths
games.skillName: Movement of the Earth and Moon and day and night
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the movement of the Earth and other planets relative to the Sun, the movement of the Moon relative to the Earth, and use the idea of the Earth's rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the Sun across the sky
games.instruction: Is each statement true or false?
games.hint: Not quite. Picture the Earth spinning and orbiting, with the Moon going round it, then try again.

questions.ask: The Earth orbits the Sun.
The Sun orbits the Earth.
The Moon orbits the Earth.
The Sun, Earth and Moon are all roughly spherical.
Day and night happen because the Sun travels around the Earth.
The Earth spins on its axis about once every 24 hours.
The Earth is flat, like a plate.
The Earth takes about one month to orbit the Sun.

games.title: Force Finder
games.skillName: Gravity, resistance forces, friction and mechanisms
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of gravity, identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, and recognise that levers, pulleys and gears allow a smaller force to have a greater effect
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which force or machine the sentence describes, then try again.

questions.ask: An apple falls to the ground because of the force of ___.
Gravity pulls unsupported objects down towards the ___.
A parachute falls slowly because of ___ resistance.
A fish's streamlined shape helps it reduce ___ resistance as it swims.
The force between two surfaces rubbing together is called ___.
A lever lets a smaller force have a ___ effect.
A ___ uses a wheel and a rope to help lift heavy loads.
___ are toothed wheels that turn each other in bikes and clocks.

games.title: New Life Steps
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals
games.instruction: Tap the step that comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what has to happen before a new plant or animal can start to grow, then try again.

questions.ask: Pollination → Fertilisation → ?
Pollination → Fertilisation → Seeds form → ?
Seeds form → Seed dispersal → ?
Bee carries pollen → Pollen lands on stigma → ?
Cut a stem from a geranium → Place it in water → ?
Plant an old potato → Shoots grow from its eyes → ?
Mammal parents mate → Baby grows inside mother → ?
Birds mate → Female lays eggs → ?

games.title: Growing Up Riddles
games.skillName: Changes as humans develop to old age
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the changes as humans develop to old age
games.instruction: Read the clues and tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how the body changes from birth to old age, then try again.

questions.ask: I drink milk, cannot walk yet and need adults to do everything for me. What am I?
I am about one to three years old and learning to walk and say words. What am I?
I go to primary school, lose my milk teeth and grow steadily. What am I?
My body is going through puberty and I am growing quickly. What am I?
I have stopped growing taller and my body is fully grown. What am I?
My hair may turn grey, my skin wrinkles and my bones grow weaker. What am I?
I am the time when a child's body changes into an adult's body. What am I?
I am the time a baby grows inside its mother before it is born. What am I?

games.title: Change Predictor
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to demonstrate that dissolving, mixing and changes of state are reversible changes, and explain that some changes result in the formation of new materials, and that this kind of change is not usually reversible, including changes associated with burning and the action of acid on bicarbonate of soda
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen.
games.hint: Not quite. Ask yourself whether a new material is made or the change can be undone, then try again.

questions.ask: What will happen if you stir sugar into warm water?
What happens when you add vinegar to bicarbonate of soda?
What will happen if you leave salty water in a warm place for a few days?
What will happen if you burn a piece of paper?
What happens when melted chocolate cools down?
What will happen if you pour sandy water through filter paper?
What will happen if you shake rice and flour in a sieve?
What will happen if you leave an iron nail in damp air for weeks?

games.title: Solution Words
games.skillName: Words for dissolving, separating and changes
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to know that some materials will dissolve in liquid to form a solution, describe how to recover a substance from a solution, and decide how mixtures might be separated, including through filtering, sieving and evaporating
games.instruction: Tap the word that matches the meaning.
games.hint: Not quite. Read the meaning again and think about what happens to the materials, then try again.

questions.ask: A liquid with a solid dissolved completely in it
Describes a material that can dissolve in a liquid
Describes a material that will not dissolve in a liquid
Separating an undissolved solid from a liquid using paper with tiny holes
Separating large solid pieces from small solid pieces using a mesh
Letting a liquid turn into a gas so a dissolved solid is left behind
A change that can be undone, such as melting or dissolving
A change that makes new materials and usually cannot be undone

games.title: Solar System Ranks
games.skillName: Comparing the Sun, Moon and planets
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the movement of the Earth and other planets relative to the Sun in the solar system, and describe the Sun, Earth and Moon as approximately spherical bodies
games.instruction: Tap the one that best answers the question.
games.hint: Not quite. Picture the planets in order from the Sun and think about their sizes, then try again.

questions.ask: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
Which planet is furthest from the Sun?
Which is the largest planet?
Which of these spherical bodies is the largest?
Which of these spherical bodies is the smallest?
Which of these takes the longest time?
Which planet takes the shortest time to orbit the Sun?
Which planet takes the longest time to orbit the Sun?

games.title: Force Lab
games.skillName: Planning fair tests on air resistance and friction
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should plan different types of scientific enquiries, recognising and controlling variables where necessary, take measurements with increasing accuracy and precision, take repeat readings when appropriate, and record data in tables
games.instruction: Tap the best answer for this investigation.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what a fair test needs and what you are measuring, then try again.

questions.ask: Which would you use to measure the force needed to drag a shoe across a mat?
Testing parachutes: which equipment times how long each one takes to fall?
In a fair test of parachute size, which one thing should you change?
In a friction test on different surfaces, what must stay the same?
Why should you repeat each parachute drop three times?
What is the best way to record fall times for five parachutes?
Bigger parachutes fell more slowly. What does this show about bigger canopies?
Testing clay boat shapes for water resistance: what must be the same for each?
